summary: Continuous batching lets an inference server admit new requests at iteration boundaries instead of waiting for a whole batch to finish. The strongest primary sources are the Orca and PagedAttention papers, with engineering writeups and talks that explain the serving implications.

sources.title: Orca: A Distributed Serving System for Transformer-Based Generative Models

summary.tldr: Orca introduces iteration-level scheduling so new requests can join a running batch as soon as a token step finishes.
summary.problem: Request-level batching wastes GPU work when sequences decode at different lengths.
summary.approach: Schedule at the iteration / token boundary and apply selective batching for transformer ops.
key_findings: Iteration-level scheduling improves throughput versus request-level batching
Selective batching keeps attention correct while batching other layers
summary.why_it_matters: This is the core idea later systems call continuous batching.

sources.title: How continuous batching enables 23x throughput in LLM inference
sources.author: Anyscale

summary.tldr: Engineering explanation of why iteration-level scheduling raises GPU utilization for decode-heavy traffic.
summary.main_argument: Static batches leave the GPU idle when short sequences finish early.
technical_takeaways: Admit new requests at token boundaries
Memory management becomes the next bottleneck after scheduling
summary.why_it_matters: Useful bridge between the Orca paper and production serving stacks.
